evals.prompt: Acme Payments is going for SOC 2 Type II, Security and Availability, for 1 April to 30 September 2027. Controls today: Google Workspace SSO with MFA, joiners requested in Linear and approved by the hiring manager, leavers removed by IT 'usually the same day' with no ticket, GitHub PR reviews required on main, GCP Cloud SQL backups nightly, an uptime status page, PagerDuty on-call run by Priya Nair (SRE lead). Map our controls to the criteria, list the evidence the auditor will want, and show the gaps as a table and a CSV.
assertions: Every common criterion and every Availability criterion in scope is either mapped to a control or listed as a gap
Each control is written as who does what, how often, and where it is recorded
Type II evidence names the full population, the system it is exported from, and what each sampled item must show
The leaver process with no ticket is marked partial or gap, not in place, because it leaves no per-sample record
Criteria IDs used are real AICPA TSC IDs (for example CC6.2, A1.2); areas without a confident ID are described in words
System, owner and frequency are given for every row, and owners not in the prompt are marked to confirm rather than invented
GCP is treated as a subservice organisation with its SOC report to collect
A CSV with one row per control-criterion pair is provided alongside the table

evals.prompt: Tillbrook Payroll Services is going for SOC 2. Our scope is in audit-scope.md, our controls are in controls.csv, and our Head of Compliance's notes are in tooling-notes.md. Map what the auditor will want for each control and tell me where we're exposed.
assertions: Treats the audit as Type II over 1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027: evidence asks cover the whole period's population or samples, and the plan to screenshot the background-check portal the week before the auditor arrives is flagged as not enough
Flags that access reviews (C02) are listed as quarterly but have been ad hoc, with the last one in February 2026
Flags that 90-day ticket history can't supply a full population of access requests (C01) and changes (C05) for a six-month period
Notes that audit-scope.md says 14 controls but controls.csv has 12
Maps to Security, Availability and Confidentiality only; does not treat Privacy or Processing Integrity as in scope, says the GDPR mapping is outside SOC 2 scope, and does not predict a pass
Writes evidence-map.csv with one row per control
Does not invent controls, systems, owners or evidence that exists; gaps such as the missing deletion log for C12 are recorded as gaps

evals.prompt: hi, i run operations at a small translation agency (9 people). our biggest client says we need SOC 2 before they renew next year. we use a cloud drive for files, email, and everyone has a company laptop. no IT person. what will the auditor actually ask us for? keep it short, like a page.
assertions: Explains in plain terms that SOC 2 is an independent auditor's report, not a certificate or a form to fill in
Explains the choice between a point-in-time report and one covering a period, and that the client's requirement decides which, without stopping to ask first
Lists evidence in terms of the tools they actually named (the cloud drive, email, company laptops), such as who has access, MFA, laptop encryption, joiners and leavers
Mentions that a few policies and written processes will be needed, and that with no IT person someone must own this
Does not invent systems, tools, vendors or costs the agency didn't mention
Stays at about one page in plain language for a non-specialist
